requiredFindings.title: Make confirmation of the existing caps consistent with the census rule
requiredFindings.description: LD-S9-5 says the procedure derives, rather than chooses, each cap as the smallest power of two at least twice its census maximum. The next step permits keeping all snapshot_profile caps whenever those derived values are merely less than or equal to them. Strict inequality selects larger caps than that rule derives. For example, a census yielding a 2^20 edge rule value does not derive the existing 2^24 edge cap. The cited R9 rule uses an exact minimum-power derivation, not an arbitrary larger existing profile. The unchanged-constructor branch therefore cannot be described as application of the stated rule or as replacing the interim with those rule-derived caps.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Require equality of all derived coordinates to confirm snapshot_profile under the stated exact rule; otherwise land the derived profile with the appropriate census-batch treatment. Alternatively, explicitly propose a different accepted rule that allows retaining an existing larger cap after a census proves its margin, distinguish census-validated reused policy from exact census-derived caps, and update the landing/control/gate text consistently. Do not silently treat a successful margin check as an exact derivation.
requiredFindings.validationExpectation: Specify controls for derived coordinates equal to, below and above the interim, including mixed-coordinate cases. The selected constructor/caps and recorded source must follow the accepted rule exactly; no constructor change may be claimed only in the equality case unless an explicit alternative retention policy is selected.

requiredFindings.title: Describe the numerical model as a partial edge boundary rather than full R10a feasibility
requiredFindings.description: The checker omits D4-1, D4-2 and all of M, and computes no byte coordinate. Its object counts exclude even the retained-slice allocations that the record itself says M needs. Nevertheless section 4 calls its values the largest sizes whose R10a edges fit, states that one R10a can verify 0.75 to 1.0 GB across the admitted set, and asserts that the object and byte coordinates stay within their caps. These full-admission claims do not follow from the reported subtotal. At each reported edge boundary the modeled subtotal already consumes all 2^24 edges, leaving no room for the omitted, nonzero D4 work. Per-component fixed costs also mean a one-component illustrative size is not a generally established capacity for arbitrary selectable sets. A reproducible subtotal is not a complete A(Sigma) bound.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Keep M owed to its owner; do not invent its price to close this review. Label the figures and output as edge-only boundaries of the explicitly named subtotal and the object figures as partial counts. Remove or qualify the full-admission, all-coordinate and arbitrary-aggregate feasibility claims. Explicitly require the priced M representation and the finalized accepted CI/D4 bounds before a complete A(Sigma) census or production fit claim; keep that completion gate distinct from acceptance of the interim policy. Extend wiring controls to exhaustion in D4-2 and M as well as the currently listed terms. Do not equate a conservative owner bound with an exact executed charge total where the owner charges actual comparisons.
requiredFindings.validationExpectation: Show that the reported subtotal is reproduced without calling it complete R10a capacity. A full-bound control must include all terms, including nonzero D4 and priced M, before asserting fit in all three coordinates. Demonstrate that a subtotal at the edge cap does not itself establish full admission, and retain multi-component aggregate exhaustion with no partial admitted set.
